messages:
akash: Quick sync — I ran a head-to-head between two kernel strategies (fat vs slim) across 4 workloads: chat-64, chat-512, embed, rerank. Replay harness + synthetic spikes. KV toggles (warm/cold) and three quant profiles: fp16, q4_0, q4_1. Need a sanity-check on methodology before I push this to the perf dashboard.

maria: Nice. Did you normalise batch policies and padding? apples-to-apples is easiest to get wrong.

akash: Yep — same batcher config: max_batch_tokens=4096, max_batch_items=16, batching_policy=latency-pref. Forced deterministic seq-len distribution by sampling from the production trace histogram. KV state seeded from the replay (so warm==prewarmed=false vs true).

tony: Can you paste the replay command you used? Want to reproduce locally.

akash: Sure:
```
./replay_harness 
  --trace=prod_replay_2026-03-09.tar 
  --kernels=slim,fat 
  --kv-mode=warm,cold 
  --quant=fp16,q4_0,q4_1 
  --batching=autotune 
  --seed=42 
  --out=artifacts/1853009999
```

jen: Quick glance at artifacts: fat kernel gives lower p95 on chat-512 when kv warm, but slim is better p50 on chat-64 and embedding paths. There's a tradeoff that looks correlated with KV hit rate.

akash: Exact numbers from the run (chat-64, kv warm):
- fat fp16: p50=18ms p95=120ms
- slim fp16: p50=14ms p95=170ms
- slim q4_1: p50=12ms p95=220ms (note: q4_1 reduces p50 but p95 balloon)

sam: Those p95 swings smell like batching jitter + KV miss tails. Did you instrument per-batch latency and KV lookup latency?

akash: Yup — added per-request trace tags and grouped by batch size. The tail events map to batches that had a mix of long-seq + cold-kv lookups. Kernel choice affects kernel startup amortisation too (fat wins when many long sequences per batch).

maria: For quality tradeoffs — any eval on hallucination/token degradation with q4_0/q4_1? We should gate quant changes on a small eval set.

jen: Ran the QA eval (50 constrained prompts): q4_1 had ~3% more divergence on our BLEU/QA pass metric vs fp16; q4_0 was within noise (~0.5%). Speculative decoding lowered average token latency by ~10% but introduced ~1% extra incorrect stop tokens on the chat set.

sam: Proposed action: 1) Add per-route regression gate that checks p95/p50 delta and quality delta; 2) Canary slim kernel + q4_0 with 5% traffic; 3) If p95 regressions >10% AND quality delta >1% block rollout. Thoughts?

tony: Sounds good. Also add a KV-hit-rate budget: if hit_rate < 85% for a route, prefer fat kernel fallback automatically. That reduces the tail.

akash: I'll add the gate logic to the rollout config. Putting a draft snippet here:
```json
{
  "route": "chat-*",
  "canary": 0.05,
  "metrics": {"p95": {"max_rel_regress": 0.10}, "quality": {"max_abs_regress": 0.01}, "kv_hit_rate": {"min": 0.85}}
}
```

perf-bot: Perf run complete: artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-perf/artifacts/1853009999. Summary: slim+q4_0 improves token-ms by 8% overall, increases p95 by 12% on long-chat workloads, quality delta (BLEU) = -0.5%.

infra-bot: Canary deploy kicked: deploy-id=canary-2026-03-18-42, targets=5% traffic for chat-64/chat-512. Watchlists created: perf-room, oncall.

maria: One more ask — let's add a lightweight synthetic test where we force homogeneous long-seq batches to quantify kernel amortisation explicitly (no KV). That will isolate kernel startup vs KV tail interactions.

akash: Good call. I'll schedule a synthetic run tomorrow and post the microbench. If nothing else we at least have a reproducible recipe for the apples-to-apples comparators.

jen: Thanks — if the canary shows >8% p95 regression, we abort and roll back automatically.

akash: Copy. Will follow up with the synthetic numbers and a PR for the rollout gate.
